EHang Will Send a Fleet of 25 Autonomous eVTOLs to Thailand
7 photos
Photo: EHang
EHang is one of the global leaders in pilotless eVTOL (electric vertical takeoff and landing) technology, having reached the finish line in terms of regulatory approvals fasters than anyone else. With its autonomous eVTOLs already operating domestically, EHang is now focusing on expanding its portfolio across Southeast Asia.
Thailand is becoming one of the most important targets for EHang, the Chinese AAM (Advanced Air Mobility) company that has fully certified its flagship, the pilotless EH216-S. EHang announced plans to deploy an entire fleet of 25 EH216-S aircraft to this country, not as part of some purchase agreement with a private operator, but for the company’s own expansion plan.
The deployment is part of a wider strategy to establish a regional hub in Thailand, intended to become the central hub for EHang’s expansion across Southeast Asia and other emerging markets. By sending those 25 aircraft to the area, EHang will have these assets and all the resources related to them at hand for all of its future regional projects.
This is meant to become EHang’s “regional fleet” that will be used across a series of operations, from market-specific flight validation to operational preparation in multiple countries in the region – and there are many such projects already planned, as part of the company’s Global Fast Track Program and AAM sandbox initiatives.
In fact, EHang is preparing for a very busy month of November on the regional side. Validation flights are scheduled to take place at Port City Colombo in Sri Lanka, in Hanoi, Vietnam, and in Putrajaya, Malaysia.
Before the end of this year, EHang will round up its Southeast Asia projects with several demonstration flights in Thailand, during an important event, the International Civil Aviation Organization (“ICAO”) AAM Symposium, taking place in Bangkok, in December 2026.
The 25 EH216-S eVTOLs that are about to be deployed in Thailand will join the already existing GD4.0 formation drones that have been previously sent there for EHang’s drone light show business. More of these drone for commercial light shows will also be sent in the near future, with plans to reach a stock of up to 10,000 units.
The Chinese EH216-S was the first eVTOL of its kind (pilotless, passenger-carrying) in the world to secure type certificate (TC), production certificate (PC) and standard airworthiness certificate (AC), all issued by the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC). This allows full commercial operations in China.
EHang is also developing and preparing to launch a long-range version, the VT35, which will expand potential applications to inter-city mobility. Meanwhile, the versatile EH216-S supports a wide range of applications across short-distance passenger mobility, emergency response, and aerial logistics.
EHang is also one of the most prolific AAM companies when it comes to international expansion, with a strong presence in emerging markets like Kazakhstan and Turkey.

Adieu, Google Maps: Magic Earth Gets Major Update With Traffic, Road Sign Improvements
14 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution/Magic Lane
I’ve said it before, and I’m going to say it again: if you’re looking for a Google Maps replacement and don’t check out Magic Earth, you’re probably skipping the best alternative. And the most recent update is just a reminder.
The application was bumped to version 9.5.7, and the update includes improvements for several key features, including how it shows traffic on the map, road signs, and weather information.
If you’re already a Magic Earth user, the first change you’ll notice after you install the update is additional traffic data you see on the screen.
The application now shows the delay for your active route right next to the remaining time in the journey info panel. You can tap this new info to see additional details, such as the next traffic jam, the distance until you’re supposed to encounter it, and the delay it adds to your ETA.
Next, you’ll also see more upcoming road signs appearing on the map. I’ve always said that this feature - no matter if it’s in Magic Earth, Waze, Google Maps, or Apple Maps - is one of the essential tools a driver should get in a navigation app. We get more time to slow down and approach an intersection more carefully, so the likelihood of a crash, even if someone else breaks the law, is much lower.
Photo: Magic Lane Magic Earth will now show not only traffic lights, but also give way signs, stops, and even crosswalks.
The application has also tweaked how it shows roadblocks. If you expand the info panel for a route, you should see all the roadblocks you’re supposed to come across when you drive. The navigation panel at the top of the screen also highlights an upcoming roadblock, along with the distance to its location. Eventually, Magic Earth offers to take a detour or keep the current route.
This update also includes smaller refinements and one big feature for Premium users. If you have a subscription, you can now see the weather on arrival, with the forecast displayed for either your next stop or the final destination. If you tap this weather info icon, you can see additional details, such as the feels-like value, wind, and humidity.
Furthermore, Magic Earth has also received a feature that others have been offering for quite some time: the option to see the ETA to the next stop instead of the final destination. You can enable this feature to see the time, distance, and ETA to the next stop, so if you have a multi-stop route, you’ll know precisely how far you are from your next stop.
The new version is available on the App Store , and if you previously enabled automatic app updates on your device, you might already be running it.

This French Tiny House Adds Cozy Details to a Family-Friendly Layout
12 photos
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois
One of the best parts about downsizing to a tiny house on wheels is that customization comes at a much more affordable cost compared to conventional housing. With regular houses, many people can’t even dream about ever living in their perfect home. A tiny house, on the other hand, can make their dream come true, even if at a smaller scale. This French tiny house acts as a beautiful foundation for a family’s dream home, filled with tiny charming details.
Tiny house Agathoise stands out immediately and is hard to forget. The beautiful red-tiled roof, coupled with the refreshingly simple exterior cladding evoke the timeless charm of French country homes. At the same time, there’s something majestic about this home’s architectural silhouette, even though it’s not an XL mobile home.
The distinctive porthole window right above the main entrance becomes a signature feature that defines Agathoise’s style. It’s one of those small decorative details that make a big difference . Suddenly, the home looks even more romantic and elegant. The black window frames also play a part in defining Agathoise’s style – they add just the right touch of visual contrast without offsetting the traditional aesthetic.
The main entrance placement highlights the home’s open layout even more – there’s a straight, uninterrupted line right from the main door to the bathroom, at the back of the house. This kind of layout creates the feel of a more spacious interior by avoiding the room dividers and bulky furniture that can fragment a small space.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois It also matters a lot that Agathoise was purposely built with numerous windows, strategically placed to bring natural light all along this straight line - dark, cramped corners are a big no-no in tiny houses, not just because they bring down the mood, but also from a practical perspective. Every inch of floor space is precious and should be used for a clear purpose, not just cluttered and forgotten.
Big, beautiful windows also draw the eye outwards, to the natural surroundings, creating the same effect of a contemporary-style indoor/outdoor design. This is how a tiny house interior feels bigger, even without the extra inches. The lounge, in particular, benefits the most from this strategic layout. Two windows on different walls open up the space, while the glazed entrance door expands the transparent effect that seems to bring the outdoors in.
Tiny Agathoise’s main entrance leads straight into a lovely, open lounge. Natural light in abundance, expansive views, and an open design make this lounge seem luxurious. Size-wise, there’s enough space for a classic living room setup, and a convertible sofa will ensure that this lounge can be used as a second bedroom. In this case, Agathoise can accommodate up to four people – one of the basic criteria for a family-friendly layout.
A wide corridor connects the lounge to the kitchen, with a small transition area that remains free at all time. The gallery shows a version of Tiny Agathoise that is fully built, but unfurnished, so that the future owners can pick exactly the kind of furnishings and finishes that they prefer for the kitchen, the loft bedroom, and the lounge.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois The kitchen leans more compact, as in many French tiny homes, which means that you won’t see the large countertop typically offered in American tiny homes. The cabinetry is also limited to lower cupboards. Two large windows make it impossible to add upper cabinets, but the advantage is undeniable – better air circulation and lots of natural light in this small kitchen.
Also, there’s no need to worry about storage. Even if there’s no room for upper cupboards or a classic pantry, Tiny Agathoise features a massive built-in staircase that is able to successfully replace traditional cupboards. You can see that the built-in storage includes full-size closets and nooks instead of the smaller, simpler open compartments of other types of staircases with built-in storage.
To make this versatile staircase even better, one of the nooks it incorporates is specifically meant to be a little pet house. It’s the only open nook carved into the staircase, and big enough to house a pet’s bed comfortably. This makes Tiny Agathoise a pet-friendly tiny house, too.
Some of the actual treads include hidden drawers as well, and most importantly, they are wide and long enough for comfortable, safe access to the loft. French tiny homes often use alternative types of staircases, especially in the more compact layouts. That’s great in terms of space efficiency, but not so great for long-term accommodation, as these are not the most comfortable staircase/ladder options.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Tiny Agathoise, however, takes the classic route when it comes to loft access, and this is another important thing to consider when looking at family-friendly layouts. The loft itself is quite spacious for this type of mobile house (seven square meters/75 square feet) and it has several features for elevated comfort. Large windows on each side ensure proper cross-ventilation and better brightness overall.
The back of the room is cleverly upgraded with built-in furniture, including cabinets and shelfs, all along the rear wall. This is a great solution for adding storage while leaving plenty of floor space for a two-person bed – this is the home’s main bedroom.
In terms of materials, the timber paneling throughout is reminiscent of traditional wooden huts; timber is one of the best natural materials, and in places like France, it doesn’t drive tiny house prices through the roof. In other words, in the case of a French tiny house, it’s a much better option overall than cheaper materials that don’t have the same properties as natural wood.
Tiny house Agathoise is presented in a lockup stage, before the final furnishing and interior décor, but its bathroom is fully equipped. Although very small, this bathroom still has its charm. An ultra-slim vanity with a small, space-saving sink sits in the center, flanked by the compact shower cabin and the toilet. A proper window brings fresh air, and tiny details like the towel rack and the mirror above the sink complete the look and functionality of this wood-clad bathroom.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois All in all, Tiny Agathoise boasts 29 square meters (312 square feet) of living space, and its 8.5-meter (28 feet) length is significantly more generous than the typical compact French homes on wheels, usually limited at around six meters (just under 20 feet).
The added floor space, the considerable storage built into the staircase, and the flexible room configuration are some of the main qualities that makes Tiny House Agathoise a family-friendly option, even though it’s still compact and frugal by US standards. Natural timber is used throughout, inside and out, which is one of the most important features that distinguishes French tiny homes from those built in the US, Australia, and New Zealand.
Mon Reve en Bois is a tiny house manufacturer operating in the famous area of Occitania. With an extensive experience of more than a decade in building mobile homes, this manufacturer also specializes in off-grid equipment and building homes on wheels that are entirely self-sufficient.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois It’s committed to using as many eco-friendly components as possible throughout the construction process, and it also relies mostly on Douglas fir and spruce sourced from sustainably-certified forests in Occitania. Also, every step of the tiny house construction process, from the initial frame to the final equipment setup is completed fully in-house, which also helps save resources and leads to overall lower costs.

You've Probably Never Seen Anything Like This Immensely-Powerful Audi RS3 Sedan, Have You? – Video
6 photos
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Extreme Acceleration TV
What’s the first thing that comes to mind when you think of the Audi RS 3 ? That it’s a great premium subcompact sporty daily? That the Sportback, aka the hot hatch version, is not available in the States? That the Sedan is just as cool as its five-door sibling?
Well, all of the above are correct, yet we can tell you that you probably do not think of this model as a supercar killer. But it is. And that’s without any outside intervention. How come, you ask? Well, it’s an older-generation supercar bully, because the newer blue-blooded models sit in a much superior league, and they are faster than ever to the point where their output and performance would have put them in the hypercar league a couple of decades ago.
Lamborghini’s Countach , which was a supercar born between 1990 and 2001, needed just 4.5 seconds in order to reach 62 mph (100 kph), according to a test conducted by Auto Motor und Sport back in the day. And that’s pretty much new-gen hot hatch territory. Don’t get us wrong, because we’d pick the classic Countach over any modern-day hot hatch (and not only), but in terms of performance, it does not make a deep statement anymore. But the thrills that it provides are definitely worth writing home about.
We didn’t mention this model for nothing, because we want to compare its performance to the Audi RS 3 Sedan. For instance, the 2023 model year car, which you can see on video at the bottom of the page, needed just four seconds flat in order to complete the 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) sprint. And that’s half a second faster than the Countach. To better put this number into perspective, we will also remind you that the Ferrari Enzo needed 3.65 seconds in order to complete the acceleration.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Extreme Acceleration TV Flat-out, the four-door did up to 174 mph (280 kph), and that’s with no outside intervention. The engine is a five-cylinder 2.5-liter with turbocharging, which pumps out 395 horsepower with zero mods. That’s 400 horsepower for the metric crowd, and 294 kilowatts. As for the peak thrust, it was rated at 354 lb-ft (480 Nm) when the car was new. Everything is channeled to the all-wheel drive system via a 7-speed automatic transmission.
As a result, this iteration of the Audi RS 3 Sedan packs plenty of punch for fun daily drives, wrapped into a premium subcompact four-door body. As for the example depicted on video at the bottom of the page, it features some ultra-fat tires wrapped around the new wheels, as well as a few other modifications, and to be honest, nothing says that it packs a jaw-dropping amount of power. But it has, and it is so much oomph available via the right pedal that it can send shivers down the spines of modern-day blue-blooded machines.
If the video uploaded, namely Extreme Acceleration TV on YouTube is correct, then this machine has no less than 1,200 horsepower. Not at the crank, but at the wheels. The car boasts countless oily modifications, and is said to tip the scales at 3,150 pounds or 1,428 kilograms. And if you want to see what it is capable of in a straight-line acceleration, then you have come to the right place, because it was demonstrated.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Extreme Acceleration TV The demonstration occurred on what seems to be a public road late at night, and we obviously do not condone this behavior, because car-related stunts should be kept away from public roads for obvious reasons. The footage, which is roughly one-minute long, does not actually reveal the 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) acceleration time, nor the top speed of this otherwise insane Audi RS 3 Sedan, as it only shows that it needed a mere 3.03 seconds in order to get from 60 to 130 mph (97 to 209 kph), according to the third-party device that recorded the run.
So, what should we understand from this? That this machine likely has too much oomph for its own good, and laying down the immense thrust is extremely tricky. Thus, its owner definitely needs to fix that, as it may be a surface-to-surface missile after taking off, but the take-off part remains controversial. Either way, with the right amount of work, this thing can actually end up giving supercars a run for their money, in a straight-line acceleration test, anyway.
Now, before inviting you to drop a few lines in the comments area below and speak your mind about this crazy Audi RS 3 Sedan, we have to tell you to click play on the video embedded at the bottom of the page, and see this machine in action. And now that you have, what is your take on the immense output, the performance, and the way it sounds?

What If Stellantis Allowed SRT To Bring Back the GTX Nameplate Based on a 1970s Plymouth – Rendering
9 photos
Photo: adry53customs / Instagram
Stellantis is currently preparing for the upcoming 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas, Nevada, and they have already revealed what’s new from Dodge – an exclusive Mopar '27 bundle available for the 2027 Charger R/T and Scat Pack Plus models to celebrate 90 years of Mopar, though only on 270 examples.
The 2026 SEMA Show is just around the corner, and, unsurprisingly, Stellantis joins the event to showcase what’s new from its variety of brands. Dodge took off with the Charger R/T and Scat Pack Plus fastback coupe variants wearing the Mopar '27 package, but we bet there will be more on offer.
Actually, the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI are also ready to contribute. For example, Timothy Adry Emmanuel, the virtual artist better known as " adry53customs " on social media, continues his dream ride periplus within the CGI car world with a focus on Stellantis lately.
Not long ago, he created the virtual Dodge Copperhead Concept to potentially bring back the Challenger in an unofficial, hypothetical design project as a longtail model specifically created to fight the likes of the Ford Mustang GTD. It was envisioned as an “update for the Challenger model but with a longtail treatment on the back,” inspired by Stellantis’ roster at the Paris Motor Show but rocking America’s muscle car style with a 1,000+ horsepower V8 powertrain and a sport chassis that would allow it to compete with the mighty GTD.
Now, he switches his attention to the defunct label Plymouth, because “after doing the longtail Challenger concept I decided to bring more American Muscle cars with longer tail and I think one of the best candidates for a modern reinterpretation is the GTX, or the Satellite, or the Roadrunner from 1971-1972.”
He imagines that his design project could be made by Dodge as the revival of the SRT GTX nameplate and in place of the Super Bee, instead rocking a Hemi V8 and Plum Crazy attire. Basically, his idea is modelled after the Plymouth GTX from 1971, an upscale mid-size muscle car based on the B-body architecture as a two-door hardtop featuring the mighty 426 and 440ci V8s of the company.
The modern reinterpretation features the same double round front lights, now in LED, the pointy front end, and even the cowl induction hood with black plastics on top of it, as well as the rectangular rear lights, now also LEDs. But the contemporary creation now has a widebody style complete with a similar profile, again blending the retro-modern cues that have become so famous as of late across the automotive industry. So, what do you think – yay or nay? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Timothy Adry Emmanuel (@adry53customs)

Range Rover Autobiography LWB Goes for $18K at Auction, SUV Was Over $152,000 New
16 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Were you somehow under the impression that you need to be loaded if you want to buy a modern Range Rover ? Well, you don’t, especially if you opt for the previous generation, because this one now goes for pennies on the dollar.
The L405 hasn’t aged badly at all, and the average Joe might look at it and say that it has to be new. Production spanned between 2012 and 2021, and this model was offered with several gasoline units, including a V8, and a few diesel engines. And it was a very big boy, measuring 204.7 inches (5,199 mm) in length in the LWB (long wheelbase) configuration, 87.4 inches (2,220 mm) in width, and 72.2 inches (1,835 mm) in height, and had 122.9 inches (3,122 mm) between the axles.
Pictured above is a 2016 Range Rover Autobiography AWD with a Santorini Black Metallic exterior and an Ebony / Vintage Tan leather interior. It rides on 22-inch (Style 707) wheels, has an active locking rear differential, and power running boards. It also features individual seats at the rear, a rear-seat entertainment system, heated, ventilated, and massaging seats with power adjustment, a panoramic sunroof, a Meridian sound system, and adaptive cruise control, among other stuff.
This long wheelbase luxury-oriented SUV packs a V8 engine under the hood. It is a supercharged 5.0-liter unit that develops 518 hp (525 ps/386 kW) and 461 lb-ft (625 Nm) of torque. This model took just under five and a half seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from zero when it was new, and had a 155 mph (250 kph) top speed. The output and thrust are channeled to all four wheels through an eight-speed automatic transmission.
Photo: Cars&Bids But what about the known flaws, you ask? Well, these include some corrosion on the underbody, curb rash on the wheels, and some chips on the outside. And to be honest, that is definitely not bad at all for something like this, is it? After all, we are talking about a 2016 model year machine that has been a daily driver, by the looks of it, ever since it left the dealership back in the day. And it has seen plenty of action over the years, as you are about to find out.
The 2016 Range Rover Autobiography AWD in question is said to have had its fuel system cleaned/serviced in July 2026, and that is also when the engine oil and filter were changed. The vehicle had 91,794 miles (147,728 km) then, and at the time of cataloging, the odometer read 92,600 miles (149,000 km). Thus, this is far from being a barely-driven example, but then again, you did not think it would have fewer miles under its belt, did you? After all, we are talking about a ride that sold for $18K.
Actually, the selling price was $18,609, as this SUV was listed for grabs on Cars&Bids as part of an online auction that recently ended. The gavel hit the table on October 29, 2026, and the vehicle was advertised at the excitement of no reserve. The seller represented the titled owner, who reportedly bought it in December 2018, and they haven’t revealed why they wanted this ride gone. The Range Rover in question was $152,241 new, as per the attached window sticker.
Photo: Cars&Bids To be honest, the selling price shouldn’t be a big surprise, because it is pretty much average for this model . And yes, that includes the Autobiography long wheelbase configuration, and the supercharged V8 engine. And it proves that one must not be loaded if they dream about buying one of these. But their bank account has to contain plenty of zeros, because this model is not exactly reliable, and when things go south, it can easily bankrupt its owner.
But you already knew that, didn’t you? After all, it’s not like it’s a surprise that Range Rovers aren’t reliable, is it? But then again, it is a very comfortable, spacious, luxurious, and head-turning ride. This one went with two pairs of headphones, a spare tire, one key, and the owner’s manual. And a new set of tires, apparently, as the rubber has 2026 date codes.
From $152,241, which was the original selling price, and $18,609, which was how much it fetched at the end of the online auction is a $133,632 difference, and it translates to almost $1.5 per mile in depreciation alone. Needless to say that the Range Rover is not for everyone, but if you feel like it is the ride of choice for you, then you must have deep pockets, as mentioned above.
Now, if you came across this 2016 Range Rover Supercharged Autobiography LWB and saw that it is advertised at no reserve, how much would you have paid for it knowing what we told you about it? And better yet, would you have bought it? You can check out this SUV in more detail here on the quoted website.

2026 SEMA Show • 2027 Dodge Charger Gets Special-Edition Package Celebrating 90 Years of Mopar
33 New Premium Diecast Collectibles to Hunt for Soon
87 photos
Photo: MINI GT
It’s interesting to see how collecting diecast cars has evolved over years. Back in 2016, I would struggle to find a way to buy Mattel’s latest premium Hot Wheels models. Now, there’s a fierce competition among emerging dealers to secure as many clients as possible.
I must have worked with 10 different companies in the past two years, and I already know who’s serious about customer service and who isn’t. These days, whenever a diecast manufacturer launches a pre-order, you’ll see a wave of posts on social media announcing the opportunity.
And every collector is free to “subscribe” to the dealer he likes working with the most. One thing’s for certain, I don’t really know that many people who have abandoned Hot Wheels entirely for the “new kids on the block”. I haven’t either, as it can be fun to explore all of the options without being tied up to one brand.
Anyway, before I show you the latest releases from the four manufacturers I’ve been paying most attention to this year, I wanted to tell you about the Hot Wheels x MoMA 1965 Porsche 911 Coupe. It seemingly appeared out of thin air, and I discovered it on Mattel Creations by accident.
It’s a brand new casting by Byran Benedict, and it’s a replica of an actual car that’s on display at the Museum of Modern Art in New York. While I think both the casting and the packaging look very nice, the asking price is slightly far-fetched for my budget. But you can get one if you don’t feel the same way. We all have a different perspective in life.
Inno64 Photo: Inno64 The Hangzhou HCFC 2026 is coming up this weekend, and Inno64 seems to have a new theme ready for the event. I’ve never played The King of Fighters before, but the concept definitely seems familiar as titles like WarGods, Virtua Fighter and Mortal Kombat were part of my library in the ‘90s.
The J’s Racing Honda S2000 is one of the most exciting replicas of the Japanese machine I know of, and I recently thought about buying the one that used to show up in Hot Version videos racing down the touge.
I’d also like a closer look at the blue and white iteration, but eBay is currently my only option for it. The GR86 is the other event-special collectible you can find in Hanghzou over the next few days.
I can’t help but wonder if this car will ever become as iconic as the S2000 . We’ll know in 10 to 20 years from now. I won’t be going after either one of the two, as I’m currently trying so save up for other projects.
Pop Race Photo: Pop Race We have a list of five new Pop Race items to look at, and only one of them is a casting that we’ve never seen before. Sadly, it’s part of the “Pocket Bunny” trend that Mattel likely started with the ‘Tooned series. Mini GT has also joined the hype train but more on that in a minute.
I guess the Pandem Pocket Bunny 34 was born out of the desire to change things up a bit, as there are so many different 1/64th-scale Skylines on the market. I’d say this is still aimed at the adult collector given the price tag, although kids coming from wealthier families might like it, too.
Anyway, you can also hunt for the yellow 32, which seems to draw inspiration from the Pennzoil-powered GT-Rs of old. Looking at the Pandem 620, two things come to mind. Firstly, I can maybe agree that it’s an accurate recreation of the real thing. Secondly, this is the least inspiring livery I’ve seen on it so far.
The Pandem EG6 is pretty cool, though, and you may have seen photos of my Idemitsu-powered one back in July. Let’s be honest for a moment here: there will only be one best-seller in this pre-order. And that’s the RWB 930 featuring the Martini tribute livery. I think I might just add my name to the list on this one although I may have already pre-ordered one of the recent Stella Artois releases.
Mini GT Photo: Mini GT The problem with all these monthly pre-orders is that you can easily lose track of them. Well, it’s not a problem if you don’t care how much you spend on the hobby, but there’s still a chance it could become a nuisance at some point. Whereas Pop Race went with the gaming approach for the show in China, Mini GT teamed up with Inozetek, a wrapping film company, for the SEMA Show .
If you’re going to the Las Vegas Convention Center between the 3rd and 6th of November, you can get either one of the two (or both) of the exclusive sets. Liberty Walk once again takes center stage, with all of the six cars inside paying tribute to Kato-san’s work.
You already know by now that I’m not a fan of the Nissan Skyline GT-R (R32) LB-Kaido Works Black, which means seeing three of them in one set does nothing for me.
There’s some diversity in the second package, as it brings together an Abarth 595, a GR Supra and the 180 SX, and I’m actually shocked to discover something like The Boring Concept exists in the first place.
Photo: Mini GT I’m definitely getting old, as I would just rather stick to the classics if you know what I mean. Qube Cars are back on the menu, and I keep telling myself I should buy one if only as an experiment.
The dealers in my area only seem to want to sell these cars in sets, which is a clear sign of their local “popularity”. There’s a choice of six models, and two of them are Porsches. I’d rather focus on the main deal. The Pandem-tuned Mazda MX-5 (NA) is the oldest car on the list. I’m almost certain it’s different from the Mint Green model we saw earlier this year, as that one doesn’t have a hardtop but features the pop-up headlights.
The Honda Prelude is the only other Japanese car on this pre-order list, and it might be too tame to bring in enough customers. Neither one of the four other collectibles in here should have that problem, especially since the Porsche 911 GT3 R and the Lamborghini Huracan most likely have a dedicated fan base behind them.
Seeing the red Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 , I can’t remember if the one I have is an older variation of the casting or the race-spec C8.R. With any luck, I’ll open it in a few weeks and then show you what it’s like. Have you ever seen an Aston Martin Valkyrie sporting a paint job like that before? I believe this is the fifth iteration of the casting, and I always wish we could open the doors.
Tarmac Works Photo: Tarmac Works Ordering online is no longer your only source for Tarmac Works collectibles. The company’s first store just opened in Hong Kong recently, and I do hope more Tarmac Grounds locations will be available worldwide within the next few years.
The latest pre-order list includes six cars, and the Mercedes-Benz SLS AMG GT3 is the only one I don’t genuinely want for my collection.
I’m stoked to see another Falken-themed Porsche 911 GT3 R, especially since I was there to see the guys driving it for the Nurburgring 24H race in 2025.
We’ve known about this Hobby64 model since circa May of this year, and I’ll be ordering one the moment I wrap up this story.
Photo: Tarmac Works The yellow and green version of the 2018 GT3 R seemed familiar, but it took me a minute to realize this Manthey Racing’s car from back in the day.
The Ferrari 458 Italia GT3 is my other favorite on this list, as I’ve followed it closely for several years when I was still in my 20s. It’s part of the Road64 collection, which makes me think it might be faster on my desktop than the Porsche.
We’ve got two rally cars on the list, and only one of them is available in Assetto Corsa Rally for now: the Audi Quattro.
This is a replica of Hannu Mikola’s Rally Argentina 1983 Winner, which means its four decades older than Sebastien Ogier’s Toyota GR Yaris Rally1 Hybrid machine. If I end up buying these two as well I might even try to set up a proper display for them in my office.

The Mercedes-AMG GT SUV Gets Rendered With Some 'Mods' Which Also Include a Switch to ICE Power
8 photos
Photo: kelsonik / Instagram
The 2027 or 2028 Mercedes-AMG GT SUV , depending on the region, has a dedicated EV architecture and no direct correspondent in the Mercedes-Benz family. It does have a 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe sibling, and while they share many things, they also strike the automotive industry as rather unique propositions for the EV segment.
The automotive world is going to receive a shock when it gets ultra-affordable EVs like the upcoming revival of the Citroen 2CV, while the roster of ultra-luxurious EVs will be much wider and more extravagant: things like the Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, or the Ferrari Luce, as well as the newly introduced Jaguar Type 01, command attention and spark controversy, while Mercedes is doubling up with the newly introduced GT SUV, too.
It won’t be without foes – like the roster of Chinese SUVs or the new Bentley Torcal, for example, but it will come with a focus on sportiness rather than outright opulence. Naturally, all these controversial models have attracted a lot of attention from everywhere, including the parallel universes of vehicular CGI thanks to the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators.
For example, Nikita Chuicko, the virtual artist better known as " kelsonik " on social media, thinks that now is the right CGI time to work on the new 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT SUV – all over again. Initially, he included the new AMG GT SUV in his new series of CGI ‘Pure Stock’ models where he takes these premium and ultra-luxury model novelties and makes them basic vehicles featuring long-forgotten affordable features like steel wheels, manual transmission, and hand-cranked windows.
However, the pixel master hasn’t stopped there and took the Mercedes-AMG GT SUV for another spin across Imagination Land – this time around giving it some CGI ‘mods.’ Those include a reworked front bumper with new side intakes, even larger Y-spoke aftermarket wheels featuring crimson brake calipers behind them, and a different setup for the rear taillights, which now feature two sets of triple horizontal LEDs instead of the round LEDs with three-pointed stars in them.
Alas, the biggest change probably comes unknown, under the hood – around the back, the diffuser also has a set of quad exhaust outlets, revealing that this unofficial, hypothetical design project isn’t an EV anymore and instead comes with ICE power under the hood – a mighty V8, for sure, since we are dealing with the GT 63 version.
What do you think? Would you choose this variant even if it comes with around half the power of the 1,153-hp electric AMG GT SUV 63 version, or are you sold on the zero-emissions model that actually comes with fake V8 engine sounds? 2026 SEMA Show • Honda Racing Releases Its First-Ever In-House Made Parts for the Civic Type R and Integra Type S
Parvati Is a Classic Italian Icon Disguised as a Bargain
28 photos
Photo: Worth Avenue Yachts
With the 67th edition of the Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show currently underway, we are reminded that so many spectacular luxury yachts in all size categories continue to appear and dazzle, adding new excitement to the market. Still, even with all of these superb luxury toys turning heads, there will always be a special place for classics, and nothing beats a true Italian classic like Parvati.
At face value, the preference for classic yachts could be considered simply a matter of taste. Connoisseurs will appreciate their quirks and even their faults, and many of them are willing to spend millions, sometime even more that what they paid for the yacht itself, to restore its classic beauty and make sure it remains seaworthy for the next decades.
Others might find classic yachts from certain eras, like the ‘70s and ‘80s, to look tacky and certainly outdated. While technologically they can be proven travelers, rugged enough to be even more reliable than younger counterparts, classic yachts have a distinctive style that people either love or hate.
Parvati falls in the same category. Some will immediately appreciate its classic gentleman’s yacht silhouette and ‘80s exterior styling, while others will only see it as a project that needs full rehabilitation. The truth is that Parvati has been searching for a new owner for quite a while. Back in 2024, it was listed for sale almost in the same condition as today, and for the same price: €2.35 million. Today, that’s the equivalent of roughly $2.6 million.
Photo: Worth Avenue Yachts It’s a bargain, considering that Parvati is presented in excellent shape, ready to sail, and upgraded following several refits. Yes, its classic ‘80s interiors haven’t really changed over the years, and perhaps they could benefit from a major transformation, but as far as performance goes (which is the most important), Parvati is in top shape.
At the time of its launch, in 1979, this Italian icon was named Santa Cruz Tres. Over the decades, its name changed multiple times, indicating several ownerships. It was never linked by the media to a famous or particularly wealthy owner, which is probably why Parvati stayed in the shadows compared to other CRN yachts from the same era. Still, its discretion doesn’t mean a lack of style.
Parvati showcases the well-known Italian elegance of the early ‘80s era in full glory, and its beautiful silhouette is a reflection of the CRN heritage – one of the most significant names in Italian yacht-building. It was the result of a collaboration between CRN and the Kirschstein Designs for exterior and interior design.
Size-wise, Parvati is not a superyacht, but closer to a classic gentleman’s yacht. An overall length of almost 110 feet (38 meters) is coupled with a 23-foot (7.1 meters) beam, an 8.5-foot (3.4 meters) draft, and internal volume of 239 GT. A classic steel hull with an aluminum superstructure strikes a balance between robustness and speed.
Photo: Worth Avenue Yachts Two CAT engines (1,200 hp) propel Parvati at a cruising speed of 12 knots, and a maximum speed of almost 15 knots. At an eco-speed of 10.5 knots, this smaller yacht can ensure a range of 5,000 nautical miles, enough for a wide range of destinations.
Throughout the years, Parvati has undergone several refits, but the most important one in its history is the 1999 visit to the French shipyard La Ciotat, where it was practically rebuilt. That is the year that marks the difference between the original Santa Cruz Tres era and the modern Parvati. Many years later, in 2014, it would undergo another comprehensive refit.
Today, as well as in 2024, when it joined the market, no other recent refits are mentioned, except for new teak added to the side decks in 2019.
Despite this being a yacht below 50 meters, it offers a similar accommodation capacity to much bigger superyachts. The difference is that it doesn’t have the same ultra-spacious outdoor areas; back then, in the early ‘80s, when the era of superyachts was just starting, owners didn’t put such an emphasis on outdoor living as today, when it’s one of the top requests for any new yacht design.
Photo: Worth Avenue Yachts Parvati can comfortably welcome 10 to 11 guests in five staterooms. The master suite has the traditional placement on the main deck, and it includes a walk-in wardrobe, a makeup vanity, and an en-suite bathroom with a bathtub and two sinks. All the guest staterooms are located on the lower deck, and two of them can be connected into a single full-beam suite, thanks to a sliding partition.
Back in the day, before designers truly mastered the outdoor living area onboard superyachts, the main salon was the most important area for socializing onboard a yacht. Parvati’s classic main salon stands out due to the 2.1-meter (6.9 feet) ceiling height, which is generous for that era, and a big influence on the overall ambiance of the salon.
In addition to the comfortable seating, there’s enough space for a huge dining area, big enough for all ten guests. The separate TV lounge, fully glass-enclosed and with expansive views of the water, is the classic and humbler format of what is called a media room today – basically, a more intimate space for socializing and relaxation.
Although modest compared to a modern superyacht’s features, Parvati offers its own kind of outdoor fun, including al-fresco dining for up to eight guests in a dedicated, shaded area on the aft deck. On the flybridge, guests have access to the traditional sun lounging area, a bar, and a barbecue.
Photo: Worth Avenue Yachts The flybridge also houses the yacht’s tender and two Jet Skis, which frees up the aft deck for al-fresco dining. There’s also no spacious beach club, just a simple swim platform for direct access to the water.
Above everything else, Parvati is one of the rare representatives of an important stage in the history of the Italian CRN shipyard. In the early ‘70s, CRN yachts gained the distinctive features that would become the brand’s signature. A bow shape inspired by fishing boats and unusual at the time became the trademark of CRN yachts, although it was mainly introduced for practical reasons, including greater safety in choppy seas.
Santa Cruz Tres was one of the memorable yachts built in that era, from the early ‘70s to the beginning of the ‘80s, alongside names like Gazzella (1974), Moneikos (1976), and Varmar (1982). One of the most emblematic CRN yachts of that same era was Fath al Khair, the 74-meter yacht custom-built for the Emir of Quatar in 1978.
In the following era, from the ‘80’s to the ‘90s, CRN would go on to build and launch one of the most innovative and impressive yachts of its time: the legendary F110, owned by Gianni Agnelli (head of Fiat and Ferrari, and one of the most important figures in Italy’s contemporary history).
Photo: Worth Avenue Yachts The F110 is considered by experts one of the ancestors of contemporary explorer superyachts. It was the first yacht ever to include floating rubber supports for lower noise levels, and anti-vibration tiles. It was the first of its size (33 meters) to have a heliport, and it was purposely beefed-up for extended cruising in the harshest weather conditions and at all latitudes.
Although not as legendary as the F110, this earlier CRN is still a collector’s item for those who appreciate classic Italian yacht design and the advantages of a smaller, slimmer yacht. Now asking $2.6 million, Parvati is worth grabbing for an elevated cruising experience in classic style.

2026 SEMA Show • Toyota Puts Snow Tracks on Five SUVs and Trucks, Unloads Them at SEMA 2026 as the Snowhunter Bunch
Prior Design Puts the Spotlight on the Cool BMW M6 Coupe With New Tuning Pack
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | priordesign
BMW officially left the grand touring game earlier this year, when it ceased production of the 8 Series . And it’s not only the regular 8er models, namely the Coupe, Convertible, and Gran Coupe that are dead, but also their full-blown M flavors.
By the looks of it, the company does not intend to launch a direct successor to these models anytime soon, and that’s definitely a pity, as these were some of the best-looking cars in their class. The same goes for the 8er’s direct predecessor, the FXX 6 Series. You do remember the F12 Convertible, F13 Coupe, and F06 Gran Coupe, don’t you? Why, of course you do. After all, it hasn’t been that long since these left the assembly line for good.
Production spanned between 2011 and 2018 at the Dingolfing factory in Germany, which is also where the last 8ers were put together. These models were related to the F10 5 Series and F01 7 Series, and as you likely recall, the same underpinnings were also utilized by the era’s Rolls-Royce Ghost , hence, the comfortable ride, especially on cars featuring smaller wheels. The powertrain family consisted of a 3-liter straight-six turbo, a 3-liter straight-six turbodiesel, and a 4.4-liter V8.
As you likely recall, the latter was used in the 650i, making 402 hp (408 ps/300 kW) and 443 lb-ft( 600 Nm) of torque in the pre-facelifted iteration, and 444 hp (450 ps/331 kW) and 479 lb-ft (650 Nm) of torque in the LCI (Life Cycle Impulse), which is Bimmer slang for facelift. The 640i base model had 315 hp (320 ps/235 kW) and 332 lb-ft (450 Nm) of torque to play with from its inline-six turbocharged lump.
Photo: Instagram | priordesign The latter hit 62 mph (100 kph) in 5.4 seconds, and the pre-facelifted and facelifted iterations of the 650i did it in 4.7 and 4.3 seconds, respectively. As for the diesel-powered 640d, it took 5.4 seconds to complete the sprint, and had 308 hp (ps/230 kW) and 465 lb-ft (630 Nm) of torque to play with from its twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter straight-six diesel engine.
Sitting at the very top of the family was the M6 . This model had 553 hp (560 ps/412 kW) available via the loud pedal and 502 pound-feet (680 Nm) of torque, and took four seconds flat to complete the 0 to 62 mph acceleration.
It’s been a while since we last wrote about this generation of the 6er / M6, but the model is now back under the spotlight courtesy of Prior Design. The tuner used the car pictured in the gallery above as a marketing tool to advertise its PD6XX Widebody Kit, which makes the entire thing look a lot more aggressive than the standard model.
So, what is new, you ask? Well, the front bumper, for one, which has been widened in order to fit the car’s more muscular nature. There are some flaps on the sides, as well as a splitter attached to it. The wheel arches are on the extremely fat side of things, and the side skirt attachments have also come from the quoted tuner’s portfolio.
Photo: Instagram | priordesign Additional upgrades on the pictured BMW M6 Coupe include the hood, the rear bumper, and the the spoiler on the trunk lid. Prior Design hasn’t mentioned the wheels, but it is obvious that these have also come from the aftermarket world. They have a glossy black look, spin around the red brake calipers, and fit the design very nicely, this writer thinks. The car sports a gray overall look with some black details here and there.
According to the quoted tuner, this body kit does not only fit the F13 Coupe version of the long-demised BMW M6, but also the F12 Convertible, and it has been designed to be offered as a complete set. The original M6 grille and the fender trims are required, if your car is a regular 6 Series and not a full-blown M model, and the wheel arches need to be cut, so Prior Design recommends professional fitting and painting.
Does this look suit the 6er / M6? Well, I think that it definitely does, as it makes it look a lot more aggressive and a bit more exotic, if I may, as it reminds me of something that would come from Liberty Walk’s portfolio. Sure, the tuner based in the Land of the Rising Sun usually creates more aggressive designs, but I dig most of those, and I also dig the way this BMW M6 Coupe looks.
The tuning bundle makes me miss these kinds of rides, and if you feel the same, then you may want to drop a comment below. Maybe someone who holds the reins at BMW sees your comment and decides to bring back the premium-oriented GT, regardless of the name, and retain the three body styles, namely the coupe, convertible, and sedan.
